 Hon'Ble Vikram D. Chauhan, J. 
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Shiv Singh, learned counsel for the opposite party
no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The present application has been filed by the applicants for quashing the summoning order dated
26.07.2023 issued by the court of Judicial Magistrate-First Chitrakoot, charge sheet dated
16.07.2023 as well as entire criminal proceeding of Case No. 3506 of 2023 (State Versus Manoj
Kumar Singh & others) arising out of Case Crime No. 269 of 2022 under Sections 498A, 323, 506
I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P Act, Police Station Kotwali Karvi, District Chitrakoot pending in the court
of Judicial Magistrate-First Chitrakoot.

sentences.text:
3.  This Court on 31.7.2025 passed the following order :-
"1.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that matrimonial dispute has been settled between the parties before the Mediation Centre of this Court on 13.7.2025.

As per the aforesaid, the total payment was for Rs. 17,75,000/-, out of which Rs.
7,75,000/- has been paid to the opposite party party no. 2 and Rs. 5,00,000/- is to be paid at the time of passing of the divorce decree.
Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that divorce petition by mutual consent has been filed and the next date fixed is 8.1.2026.

2. Learned counsel for both the parties submits that Family Court, Chitrakoot may be directed to prepone the proceedings in terms of the settlement reached before this Court and the divorce decree order may be passed subject to deposit of Rs.
5,00,000/- before the Family Court, Chitrakoot by the applicants.

3. In view of the aforesaid, the Family Court, Chitrakoot is directed to prepone the proceedings of the divorce petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act in terms of the compromise reached between the parties and the divorce decree order may be passed on deposit of Rs. 5,00,000/- before the Family Court, Chitrakoot by the husband.
Application for divorce by mutual consent filed be disposed of within a period of one month by the Family Court, Chitrakoot.

4. List this case on 4.9.2025 in top ten cases.
5.

Interim order granted earlier is extended till the next date of listing."
4.

Learned counsel for the parties submits that in pursuance to the order dated 31.7.2025 divorce decree by mutual consent has been passed on 26.8.2025 and learned counsel for opposite party no.
2, Sri Shiv Singh, submits that amount of Rs. 7,75,000/- and Rs. 5,00,000/- has already been received by opposite party no. 2.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the applicants has produced bank draft of Rs. 5,00,000/- dated 30.8.2025,
bearing no. 128644, in favour of opposite party no. 2-Nisha towards the final payment of compromise as the compromise was to the tune of Rs. 17,75,000/-.
The demand draft has been handed over to learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 who has accepted the same.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that divorce by mutual consent has been granted by order dated 26.8.2025 passed by the Family Court, which is annexed at page no. 22 of the supplementary affidavit and in view of the divorce decree, the present case be finally decided.
7.
Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has not disputed the facts as stated by learned counsel for the applicants.
He further contended that opposite party no.2 does not want to proceed with the criminal case against the applicants and the same may be quashed.
8. Learned AGA does not dispute the fact that parties have entered into settlement which is duly verified by the court concerned.
It is further submitted that he would have no objection in case criminal proceedings are put to an end.
He further submits that in view of settlement there is virtually no chance of any conviction being recorded in the criminal proceedings.

9. Having examined the matter in its totality, this Court is of the view that the criminal proceedings in the present case had essentially been an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and there are no such over bearing circumstances for which the applicants ought to be prosecuted even after the parties has entered into a settlement.

Needless to observe that with the present stand of the parties in terms of their settlement, there is practically no chance of recording conviction, even if the case under the F.I.R. in question is put to trial.
In other words, entire exercise of trial would only be an exercise in futility.

On the contrary, looking to the nature of dispute and the fact that the disputants have compromised and want to proceed peacefully ahead, it would be in the interest of justice that criminal proceedings in question are quashed.

10. It would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice,
it is appropriate that the criminal case is put to an end.

11. In view of the fact that the parties do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them and the fact that matter has been mutually settled between the parties in view of the divorce decree order dated 26.8.2025 passed by the Family Court, no useful purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter further.

12. In terms of the settlement reached between the parties no future claim would arise between the parties in respect of maintenance or any other matter and all the cases pending between the parties including NCR lodged at Lucknow in Crime No. 343 of 2021 lodged by the applicants would as per learned counsel for the parties be withdrawn/quashed at the instance of the parties.
